title: Rajendra Jakkal & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (Joshi-Abhyankar Serial Murders)
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Bombay / Sessions Court Pune
source: Supreme Court of India Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1446210)
ipc_sections: Section 394 IPC (Voluntarily causing hurt in robbery)
evidence: Recovery of stolen antique jewelry, silverware, and cash buried in tin boxes at suspects' studios
Nylon ropes and chemical dismemberment agents recovered from art workshop premises
Fingerprints matching suspects found on cupboards, door frames, and telephone receivers in Joshi and Abhyankar residences
Detailed testimony of approver Kiran Soni explaining the conspiracy, planning, and weapon acquisition
Handwriting analysis on pawn shop pledge tickets signed by accused under pseudonyms
modus_operandi: Group of college students gained entry into homes of affluent families by posing as couriers, college acquaintances, or visitors. Subdued occupants using nylon ropes, administered alcohol and sedatives, strangled victims systematically, looted valuables, and wiped down crime scenes to eliminate traces.
personality_disorder: Psychological analysis presented at trial: Group-induced sociopathy, hedonistic material obsession, moral desensitization, and sensation-seeking behavior among educated youth without prior criminal records.
common_traits: Entry under deception / pretext of delivery
Simultaneous binding and gagging of multiple family members
Systematic ligature strangulation using nylon cords
Disposal of victims' bodies in gunny sacks or iron barrels
Financial looting to fund lavish lifestyle
summary: Infamous Pune serial murders of ten individuals between January 1976 and March 1977 carried out by four commercial art students. The Supreme Court affirmed death sentences for all four principal accused, highlighting the cold deliberation and absence of remorse.
